cells.tense: You're building the frame that holds the work, and you know you're the one holding the pen.
cells.ask: offer up one piece of the structure for someone to carry with you — let it come back changed and still sound.
cells.core:
You're the one setting the shape of things, and it's landing. You build frames other people can actually work inside — not cages, containers. A week has a rhythm because you gave it one, a project has edges because you drew them, and people move through what you made without having to ask where anything is. What you make holds because you made it patient instead of fast.

There's a private practice under all of it, and it's been keeping you steady. You're allowed to let it do more than that. Hand one piece of what you've built to other hands and let it stay useful there, out of your sight. Quiet work feeding a shared one — that's what this balance is free to carry next.
cells.sheetLine: You set the shape of the work, and it holds because you built it patient.
cells.verb: forcing real change into the world through patient, unstoppable building

cells.tense: You're already braced against a future where the structure has to be perfect before anything can stand in it.
cells.ask: tell one person what the structure is for, in plain words, and let their version of it change yours.
cells.core:
When this is going well, you build the frame the work can actually land in — real edges, real sequence, a shape other people can walk into and start moving. You're the one who makes it possible for a thing to happen instead of stay an idea, and you do it steadily, without drama.

Right now you're laying all of that ahead of the thing it's meant to hold. Every gap gets closed in advance, every load predicted, and the building has stopped waiting for the world it was supposed to serve. What you're making is real, but it's being made for a future that hasn't arrived and won't match your plan. Say out loud what the whole thing is for — to one person, in words they'd actually use. Their version will disturb yours. That disturbance is the point. Meaning that moves between people is what keeps a frame from turning into a wall.
cells.sheetLine: You're building for a future that can't be written in.

cells.tense: You stopped building the frame, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: set one boundary this week — a clear no or a clear yes — and let that be the first stone back.
cells.core:
You know how to give a thing a shape that holds. You've done it — laid out how a week runs, decided what belongs where, made a mess into something someone could work in. That capacity is still in you; it just isn't moving. There's a door behind you where the structure got set down, and standing still has started to feel like the whole story instead of a pause in it.

Start with one edge. A boundary you've been leaving soft. Say it plainly once, to whoever it concerns, and mean it. Not the whole frame yet — one clear line, placed where you actually want it. Things start making sense around you the moment you decide where they end.

cells.tense: You're already shaping how things run, and you talk about it like it's happening on its own.
cells.ask: claim one pattern you've been keeping — say out loud that you're the one who set it.
cells.core:
You set the pattern others work inside — that's what you do when it's going well: you take a tangle and give it a shape people can move through, and the shape holds because you keep tending it. The routine a team runs on, the order a week falls into, the way a hard conversation stays workable. You made those. They don't run without someone deciding.

Right now you keep deciding and won't say so. The deciding is real; the naming of it isn't. Pick one structure you keep in place and say plainly that it's yours — not the function, not the role, you making the call. What you tend stays lit when you know you're the one holding the match.
